name: Girls Against Boys
label: Touch and Go
lede: Girls Against Boys started as studio tinkering between Eli Janney and Fugazi's drummer, picked up a singer and a second bass, and made three records for Touch and Go that got them on late-night TV and the UK chart. Then Geffen signed them and told them, mid-tour, that it was about to stop existing.

eras.title: A side project that kept going
eras.text: Brendan Canty of Fugazi and Janney wanted a place to make music that didn't have to sound like post-hardcore. Scott McCloud came over from Soulside to sing, and when Soulside ended, its rhythm section followed him in.

years.big: "I wanted to sing about going out at night, and capitalism, and drinking culture."
years.src: Wikipedia: Girls Against Boys · Joyzine · Louder: Scott McCloud
years.h: Skind finds a singer in Scott McCloud
years.p: Janney and Canty are cutting studio tracks as Skind when Soulside's guitarist joins to sing, and a 1989 session yields three songs Wikipedia files as industrial disco. McCloud told Louder what the project let him write about.
years.xp:
The name they settled on, Girls Against Boys, was a reflection on ordinary gender rivalries, per Wikipedia. McCloud described the start to Joyzine: "It was really an evolution...a studio project consisting of Eli, Brendan Canty and I."

Canty was drumming for Fugazi at the same time, which is why he left in 1990. McCloud has said he and Janney bonded over Wax Trax records and Big Black.

years.h: Soulside breaks up and its rhythm section follows McCloud
years.p: Bobby Sullivan ends Soulside in 1990. Bassist Johnny Temple and drummer Alexis Fleisig try a short-lived band, Little Baby, with [[Mike Fellows|58a7226f-e06a-4728-82a5-ddc4443025a4]] of [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]], then join Girls Against Boys.
years.xp: Little Baby played only a handful of shows. Canty, whose main band was Fugazi, left Girls Against Boys around the same time.

years.h: One record, two bands, sorted by decade
years.p: The 1989 disco session fills the "Eighties" side of Nineties vs. Eighties; three harder songs cut in early 1990 fill the "Nineties" side. It first came out on Janney's novelty label, Slate Records.
years.xp: It was later reissued on Adult Swim Records. By the time it came out, Canty had gone back to Fugazi full time, and McCloud, Temple and Fleisig had talked Janney into leaving Florida for New York.

years.h: Luke Wood quits mid-album for the music business
years.p: Wood plays guitar in the band briefly, then leaves during the first album sessions to work in labels and lead his own band, Sammy. Seven years later he signs Girls Against Boys to Geffen.
years.xp: His guitar parts stayed on Tropic of Scorpio after he left.

eras.title: New York, with a second bass
eras.text: Janney left Florida at the urging of the other three, and the engine locked in: Temple on bass, Janney on a second bass plus keyboards and samples. Producer Ted Niceley and Touch and Go turned that into Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby.

years.h: Fugazi takes them on their first big U.S. tour
years.p: Now based in New York with Janney back from Florida, the band spends early 1992 opening for [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] across the country, which puts their former drummer, Brendan Canty, on the other side of the stage.
years.xp: The clip is a full set from January 29, 1992, from this run.

years.src: Wikipedia: Girls Against Boys · Trouser Press
years.h: Tropic of Scorpio arrives on Adult Swim Records
years.p: Janney produces it himself. Nathan Larson of [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]] guests, and Wood's guitar parts stay on the record though he's gone.
years.xp: Trouser Press hears "jazzy atmospherics" and a fluttering trumpet on Everything I Do Seems to Cost Me $20, and a "lounge-singer-on-'ludes motif" across the record, with Wow Wow Wow and Plush supplying the aggression.

years.src: Wikipedia: Girls Against Boys · Trouser Press · Louder: Scott McCloud
years.h: Touch and Go gets a record with two basses on it
years.p: Producer Ted Niceley, whose studio Janney had worked in as an assistant in the 1980s, makes Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby. It later lands in the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.
years.xp:
Trouser Press credits Janney as "Mr. Silas Greene" on bass and hears the two basses as a spin-cycle churn that sounds like Kraftwerk. McCloud's lyrics, it says, sit in Times Square squalor after his move to New York.

McCloud told Louder the title came from a flashing ad for a late-night "sexy" TV show in Spain. He says he writes from late-night bar talk, phrases overheard and repeated until they start to sound like slogans.

years.h: A Lollapalooza side stage, then the road with the Jesus Lizard
years.p: After the 1993 Lollapalooza side stage come runs with [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]], [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] and [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]], a Touch and Go labelmate.

eras.title: Sex rock on an indie budget
eras.text: Three Touch and Go albums between 1993 and 1996 took them to The Jon Stewart Show, a Clerks soundtrack and the UK singles chart. Spin ranked the last of them the fifth-best album of 1996, and that was the peak.

years.h: "Kill the Sexplayer" ends up in Clerks
years.p: Kevin Smith's film puts the song on its soundtrack. The band fills the gap before its next album with the single "Sexy Sam" and plays the Lollapalooza side stage a second time.
years.xp: Smith used them twice. "Cruise Your New Baby Fly Self" is in his next film, Mallrats (1995), and on its soundtrack. The CD of "Sexy Sam" also pulled together tracks from the band's first three releases.

years.src: Wikipedia: Girls Against Boys · Trouser Press
years.h: Cruise Yourself reaches the UK rock top ten
years.p: Niceley produces again. The album hits No. 9 on the UK Rock & Metal Albums chart, and "(I) Don't Got a Place" scrapes the UK singles chart at No. 91.
years.xp: Alternative Press and Rock de Lux liked it. Trouser Press was less sold: it found McCloud's persona had become "a shtick" and the straight rockers tepid.

yt: Live on The Jon Stewart Show, 1995
years.h: Their TV debut is The Jon Stewart Show
years.p: In January 1995 they play "(I) Don't Got a Place" and "Kill the Sexplayer". They come back in May for "Raindrop" and "Cruise Your New Baby Fly Self".

years.h: A Joy Division tribute track makes the UK chart
years.p: Girls Against Boys cover [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]]'s "She's Lost Control" for the compilation A Means to an End. Released as a single with a video, it peaks at No. 98.
years.xp: Joy Division leads the list when McCloud talks about where the band came from. He has named "avant-garde English punk bands, like Joy Division" as the primary cues, plus Big Black, Einstürzende Neubauten, Skinny Puppy, Sonic Youth and Killing Joke. The Fall and the Velvet Underground shaped how he sings.

years.src: Wikipedia: Girls Against Boys · Trouser Press
years.h: Spin puts House of GVSB fifth among the albums of 1996
years.p: Recorded in late 1995 with Niceley, the third Touch and Go album reaches No. 76 in the UK. "Super-Fire" gets to No. 82, their best UK singles showing, and No. 36 on the UK dance chart.
years.xp:
Trouser Press, which was hard on Cruise Yourself, liked this one: the creepiness "sounds earned instead of put-on," and the twin-bass attack is "so ferocious." Kerrang and Sounds praised it too.

The band played "Super-Fire" and the second single, Disco Six Six Six, on 120 Minutes and the French show Nulle Part Ailleurs.

years.h: Third and last Lollapalooza, after a run with Rage Against the Machine
years.p: Earlier in 1996 they tour with [[Therapy?|85226286-349a-4046-8dcf-f75b32baa6b1]] and [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]]. They also play HFStival in Washington and England's Reading Festival.

eras.title: Geffen calls, then Geffen goes
eras.text: Labels followed them around, and the band finished its Touch and Go commitment before answering. Geffen signed them through their own ex-guitarist, the record took six months, and the label was swallowed in a merger.

years.h: Janney spins records in New York while the band plays sparingly
years.p: He works as a DJ and remixes [[Sneaker Pimps|696d8523-39a0-44e2-9add-afaa183a2f46]] and Ruby. The band plays only a few shows, among them the first Fuji Rock Festival in Japan, and Spin lists it No. 38 on its Most Vital Artists.
years.xp: The DJ side job grew out of the 1996 tours, where the band had fallen for electronic and industrial acts on the same bills. "Super-Fire" also turned up in the 1997 film Love God.

years.big: "Buying us rooms in 5 star hotels, which was crazy, because we were still playing punk rock squats in Italy."
years.h: Geffen signs them through their ex-guitarist
years.p: Luke Wood, now a Geffen executive, makes the approach for the label. The band has just finished its three-album Touch and Go commitment, and recording with producer Nick Launay begins in October 1997.
years.xp: Several majors had been after them. The band held off to finish the Touch and Go deal first, which McCloud says only made the labels go "more crazy for us." Wood had left the band in 1990; seven years later he was on the Geffen side of the table.

years.h: Six months in the studio, after one or two for every record before
years.p: Freak*on*ica, the Geffen debut, hits No. 11 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart. "Park Avenue" gets to No. 28 on Mainstream Rock and No. 83 in the UK.
years.xp:
Entertainment Weekly, Spin and Pitchfork praised it; Rolling Stone and The A.V. Club did not. The band headlined through 1998, then went out with Garbage, and played Reading and Pukkelpop in Belgium.

"EPR" went on the Permanent Midnight soundtrack, and "Park Avenue" and "Psycho-Future" landed in the 1999 game Test Drive Off-Road 3.

years.h: GVSB play Conan and show up on screen in 200 Cigarettes
years.p: They cover "Boogie Wonderland" for that film's soundtrack, put "Psycho-Future" on the Psycho remake soundtrack and perform "Park Avenue" on Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

years.h: The Garbage tour brings news: no more Geffen
years.p: Freak*on*ica is their best seller yet but short of Geffen's targets. Seagram then buys the label, and McCloud hears on the tour that Geffen will cease to exist on January 1, 1999.
years.xp:
After a short 1999 tour with Firewater, the band sat in limbo while Universal, Geffen's parent, restructured. For almost two years it could barely record or tour. It began demoing a new album for early 2000.

At one point the band moved to Interscope, then left it after what Wikipedia calls various conflicts.

years.h: GVSB scores the film Series 7
years.p: Most of the soundtrack to the reality-TV satire is theirs, recorded in 2001. Late that year they sign with the indie label Jade Tree after the major-label detour.

years.h: Niceley returns for the Jade Tree album
years.p: "Basstation" is the only single. The band headlines a tour with the [[Yeah Yeah Yeahs|584c04d2-4acc-491b-8a0a-e63133f4bfc4]] opening; after Australia, Eli Janney sits out Europe for a family emergency and [[Sohrab Habibion|6e133bae-8f26-4f44-b1a1-622e051630be]] of Edsel fills in.
years.xp: "All the Rage" from the album ended up in the snowboarding game Amped 2 the next year.
play: You Can't Fight What You Can't See

eras.title: A band in bits and pieces
eras.text: No label and no new album, but they never fully stopped: a turn as an actress's backing band, an anniversary party, short European runs each February. In early 2009 they went quiet for four years.

years.h: Gina Gershon hires them as her backing band
years.p: Without Janney, the band tours the U.S. behind her film Prey for Rock & Roll, in which she plays an aging punk singer. The tour is filmed for the series Rocked with Gina Gershon (2004).

years.h: Brainiac's John Schmersal covers Janney's parts in Europe
years.p: [[John Schmersal|9f0f837b-e427-4611-aef4-5db88298bfaf]], also of [[Enon|ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06]], plays keyboards and bass on a short February tour. He stands in for Janney again in 2013 and 2026.

years.cap: Scott McCloud singing at the Touch and Go 25th Anniversary Block Party, Chicago, September 8, 2006
years.h: Touch and Go throws itself a 25th birthday party in Chicago
years.p: Girls Against Boys play the label's anniversary block party. The same year they play all of Venus Luxure No. 1 Baby at All Tomorrow's Parties in London.
years.xp: European tours followed each February in 2007 and 2008, with Primavera Festival in 2007.

years.cap: McCloud and a guitarist at the Touch and Go 25th Anniversary Block Party, Chicago, September 2006
years.h: After Russia, four years of nothing
years.p: Girls Against Boys play Russia for the first time in February 2009. After that there are no shows, releases or updates until 2013.
years.xp:
There was no announced breakup. McCloud later told Stereogum: "I thought, 'OK, that's probably it, we probably won't do anything anymore.'"

The members kept busy. McCloud and Fleisig started Paramount Styles in 2007 and made three albums, and Temple ran Akashic Books.

eras.title: The long tail of the House
eras.text: An email about writing songs became a reunion, an EP and an unhurried second life. Meanwhile Janney took over a late-night TV band and Temple kept a publisher and a punk supergroup going.

years.big: "If we're gonna do a song, why don't we make it a Girls Against Boys song?"
years.h: Eleven years on, a reunion falls out of an email thread
years.p: McCloud told Stereogum it started with him and Janney trading emails about writing together. "It's a Diamond Life", announced April 24, 2013, is the band's first new song since 2002.
years.xp:
McCloud said of the first sessions back: "We settled right back into our form, basically, right where we had left off." Expectations were "almost gone completely," he said, so the music "can just be what it is."

The tension hadn't gone anywhere either: "There's always this tension with us...it's exactly the same as it was before. But now I see it differently."

years.h: The Ghost List is the first new release since 2002
years.p: The EP comes out September 24, 2013, self-released with the internet label Epitonic. That month the band plays the Black Cat's anniversary show in Washington, with Schmersal filling in for Janney.
years.xp: A longer European tour and several U.S. dates came first that summer, and more U.S. dates followed in December. McCloud was living in Vienna by then, with an apartment kept in New York.

years.h: Janney becomes bandleader on Late Night with Seth Meyers
years.p: He plays keyboards and is musical director of the 8G Band. Temple, meanwhile, runs Akashic Books, the Brooklyn publisher he founded in 1997.
years.xp:
Janney had been a full-time producer since 2003, for acts including Obits and James Blunt. Akashic is behind Go the Fuck to Sleep and Hairstyles of the Damned.

The band went quiet from early 2014 into late 2016, then came back briefly for Riot Fest and Sound on Sound Fest.

years.cap: Girls Against Boys at Baby's All Right, Brooklyn, September 13, 2016
yt: Full show, Lucerna Music Bar, Prague, May 11, 2017
years.h: McCloud turns 50 in Prague, with the band behind him
years.p: The band plays only two shows in 2017: Lucerna Music Bar in Prague for McCloud's 50th birthday, and a release party for a [[Brainiac|8db9ae5b-4412-434a-aedd-dc2bb316c355]] documentary.
years.xp: After those two dates the band went inactive again. McCloud and Fleisig put out the Paramount Styles album Distant Karma that year on Silver Rocket, and McCloud had already released a solo live album recorded in Prague, Dobeška 170910.

years.h: Temple starts Fake Names, with Refused's singer up front
years.p: The band is Johnny Temple with [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]], [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] and [[Dennis Lyxzén|d7bb37a5-3d48-4a2f-a761-fe66d5cdb409]], and its debut is on Epitaph. Brendan Canty, Girls Against Boys' original drummer, plays on the 2021 EP.
years.xp: Baker's past is Minor Threat and Bad Religion, Hampton's is the Faith and S.O.A.

years.cap: House of GVSB, reissued by Touch and Go in 2022
years.src: Wikipedia: Girls Against Boys · Louder: Scott McCloud
years.h: House of GVSB gets a reissue, and the band goes back on the road
years.p: Announced in August 2021 with U.S. tour dates, the May 2022 Touch and Go reissue adds B-sides and outtakes. They tour the U.S. and Europe behind it all year.
years.xp:
McCloud told Louder how the band's start felt to him: "Do I dare to say these words?" He called letting go of inhibitions "almost euphoric." The 2022 run ended with UK and Ireland dates in Dublin, Nottingham and London in early December.

On a new record, he would only say, "something might come of it."

years.src: Wikipedia: Girls Against Boys · Louder: Scott McCloud
years.h: Japan with Soulside, the first trip there since 1997
years.p: The April tour pairs Girls Against Boys with [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], McCloud's first band, which has never played Japan.
years.xp: Soulside's A Brief Moment in the Sun came out on Dischord after 33 years, per the Louder interview.

years.h: A Cruise Yourself remaster sends them back to Australia
years.p: The band returns in February to mark the remastered album, out digitally and on vinyl. John Schmersal stands in for Janney once more.

sources.title: Washington Post: Getting Together With Girls Against Boys (1996)
